Routine labs (CBC, electrolytes, LFTs, thyroid) are normal, making reversible metabolic or endocrine causes unlikely. The clinical picture—early and prominent behavioral disinhibition, loss of social propriety, impaired executive function and language, with frontal/temporal atrophy—is most consistent with behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). Alzheimer disease is less likely because early memory impairment and hippocampal-predominant atrophy are not the dominant features here; vascular dementia is unlikely given lack of strokes on imaging and a more stepwise decline is not reported. Primary psychiatric illness is less likely given progressive cognitive decline, objective neuropsychological deficits, and structural atrophy on MRI. Therefore the single most likely diagnosis is behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD).

DIAGNOSIS: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD).
